Playbook.name: Potential Destribution Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK - T1498 Network Denial of Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense reported a distributed flood (threat category "DDoS Botnets" and/or volumetric flood classes) from many sources against a JCB internet-facing banking service. Triage question: is this an active distributed denial-of-service threatening availability, or distributed botnet-reputation traffic that AED is blocking with no service impact?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A DDoS against Internet Banking, mobile or web services can take a customer-facing service offline - a direct availability, financial and reputational impact, and a common cover for concurrent intrusion activity. Confirming scale, distribution and whether AED/upstream mitigation is holding is the priority.

Assets.AssetType: JCB internet-facing banking services behind NETSCOUT AED (bank range 91.223.202.0/24 - Internet Banking, mobile, OWA and web properties in AED protection groups, e.g. "TEJARI WEBSITE", "JCB Mobile ICS", "NEW OWA ONPREM", "Corporate Online")

LogSources.LogSource: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense CEF - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: NETSCOUT AED CEF (verified live on JCB). Populated fields: source.ip, source.geo.country_name, source.as.organization.name, destination.ip, destination.port, cef.name, cef.device.event_class_id, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 (protection group / bank service), cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 (threat category, incl. "DDoS Botnets" / "DNS Flood"), cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 (AED host score), cef.severity.

Population caveat (verified on JCB): the web-oriented fields in this rule's investigation set (cef.extensions.requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceHostName, deviceCustomString1/4/5) and event.action are typically null for NETSCOUT AED events - distribution is measured from distinct source.ip / source.geo.country_name / source.as.organization.name against the target.

Signal.Name: Distributed Flood Against a Bank Service
Signal.Details: A surge of flood / botnet-reputation events from many distinct sources against a protected bank service.

Input.name: $srcip
Input.description: One source IP participating in the flood the alert fired on (source.ip - alert entity / a single participant).

Input.name: $target
Input.description: Targeted bank asset under attack (destination.ip). The primary pivot for measuring distribution.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance - source distribution, volume, flood/threat class and whether AED is blocking with no impact - not any single fact. The defining DDoS signal is many distinct sources across many countries/ASNs against one target.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm whether the targeted bank asset is under a distributed flood (many sources/countries/ASNs), quantify its scale and composition, and establish whether AED mitigation is holding.

Step.name: The participating source's role in the flood
Step.Purpose: Characterise the alert's source IP: how much it contributed, which target(s) and services it hit, its threat/flood class and origin.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), targets = VALUES(destination.ip), services = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2), threat_cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), flood_classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), country = VALUES(source.geo.country_name), asn = VALUES(source.as.organization.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: In a DDoS each source is typically low-volume; the weight is in the aggregate. A "DDoS Botnets" threat category or a flood class here confirms the source's role. Note which bank service (deviceCustomString2) it targeted, then pivot to the target in Step 2.

Step.name: Distribution against the targeted asset (the DDoS signature)
Step.Purpose: The decisive measurement: how many distinct sources, countries and ASNs are hitting the target - the defining distributed signal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND destination.ip == "$target" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), distinct_sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip), distinct_countries = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.geo.country_name), distinct_asns = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.as.organization.name), service = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2), threat_cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct_sources across many distinct_countries/ASNs against one target = a distributed attack (confirmed DDoS). Grounding: live JCB "DDoS Botnets" activity against a single bank IP has been observed from ~180 distinct sources across ~20 countries in a 4h window. A single/handful of sources means it is a DoS, not a DDoS - use the DoS playbook.

Step.name: Attack composition - top source countries and flood classes
Step.Purpose: The geographic and flood-class composition shows the botnet footprint and the attack vectors AED is mitigating.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND destination.ip == "$target" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip) BY source.geo.country_name, cef.device.event_class_id | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A broad spread of source countries with reputation/flood classes ("Filter List"/"ATLAS Threat Categories"/rate-based) is the botnet footprint. Confirm AED is blocking these and check the targeted service's availability directly - reputation blocking with no measurable impact is routine; availability degradation is the escalation trigger.

Node.Condition: Many distinct sources across many countries/ASNs flooding a real bank service (INV-02), with volume threatening availability and AED/upstream mitigation engaged or strained.
Node.Result: True Positive (DDoS Attack - engage DDoS response, confirm mitigation and upstream scrubbing)

Node.Condition: The target is hit by only one or a few sources (not distributed).
Node.Result: Needs Escalation / Reclassify as DoS (use the DoS playbook and response)

Node.Condition: Distributed botnet-reputation traffic that AED is fully blocking with no measurable service impact, or an authorised distributed load/synthetic-monitoring test.
Node.Result: False Positive (proven-blocked distributed noise, or authorised test)

Node.Condition: A distributed flood is confirmed but scale, impact or mitigation status cannot be established, or availability is degrading.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised or proven-blocked event - distributed botnet-reputation traffic AED blocked with no service impact, or an authorised distributed load/synthetic-monitoring test. Never classify simply as "benign".

Indicators.Item: AED blocked every event (e.g. reputation "Filter List"/"ATLAS Threat Categories") and the targeted service stayed fully available.
Low aggregate volume despite source spread, or traffic that maps to a known load test / CDN health-check fan-in.
No measurable latency or error-rate change on the targeted service.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm no availability impact and/or the authorised test; document; close as proven-blocked or authorised. Keep the source list for blocklist enrichment.

TruePositive.Definition: An active distributed denial-of-service: many distinct sources generating flood traffic that threatens a bank service's availability.

Indicators.Item: High distinct-source count across many countries/ASNs against one target (INV-02).
Volumetric flood classes and/or "DDoS Botnets"/"DNS Flood" categories, with AED/upstream mitigation engaged.
Measurable service degradation (latency, error rate, saturation) on a customer-facing service.

SOCAction.Item: Engage DDoS response; confirm AED mitigation is holding and activate upstream/ISP scrubbing; monitor service availability; watch for concurrent intrusion activity using the DDoS as cover.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the targeted service and whether it is degraded or down; check availability directly.
Confirm distribution and scale from INV-02/INV-03 (distinct sources, countries, flood classes).
Verify AED mitigation is engaging and determine whether upstream/ISP scrubbing must be activated.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Engage DDoS response; confirm AED mitigation is holding; activate upstream scrubbing / ISP coordination for volumetric floods; monitor availability; hunt for concurrent intrusion activity masked by the flood.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune AED protection thresholds for the affected service; validate upstream scrubbing capacity and runbooks; feed the source/ASN footprint into blocklists; document the attack for capacity planning.

Escalation.Trigger: Confirmed distributed flood with service degradation/outage, mitigation not holding, a single/few-source pattern (reclassify as DoS), or signs of concurrent intrusion using the DDoS as cover.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Proven-blocked distributed noise or authorised test confirmed; no availability impact; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: DDoS mitigated (AED + upstream scrubbing); service availability restored and verified; no concurrent intrusion found; attack footprint documented for capacity planning and blocklisting.
